en: The Scripture on the Divine Incantation for Securing One’s Dwelling, Spoken by the Buddha;
translated during the Later Han Dynasty, the name of the translator lost.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
Together with twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
all of whom were arhats whose outflows were exhausted,
their bodies and minds were serene and pure, and they possessed the six supernormal powers without obstruction.
Their names were the Greatly Wise Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana,
Mahākāśyapa, Mahākātyāyana, Subhūti, and others.
There were also eight thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas present together with them.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, the Guide Bodhisattva,
Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, and Trāṇamukta Bodhisattva—
such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as these possess sovereign majesty and power.
Furthermore, there were bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās,
together with devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and the eight classes of spirits, all surrounding him as he preached the subtle and wondrous Dharma.
At that time, there were fifty Licchavi elders' sons together with him;
their bodies were covered in dust and they were filled with sorrow and grief,
like people who have lost their parents, their loved ones, or their wives and children.
They approached the Buddha, prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, and withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the reason, asked them intentionally:
"Sons of elders, for what cause and condition do you have such a troubled appearance?"
Filled with sorrow and lacking joy, he lost his usual composure.
At that time, the sons of the elders spoke to the Buddha with one voice, saying:
"World-Honored One, we do not yet understand how a person dwells in this world."
"Are there indeed matters of good and bad fortune regarding one's household?
The Buddha replied, "It is so.
All such matters arise from the mental conduct of sentient beings."
That which is created by dreams cannot be entirely non-existent.
The Licchavis and others addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, your disciples have received even a hair’s breadth of merit from their past conditions."
I have been able to behold the Tathāgata’s compassionate transformation, leaving no one behind;
he has opened the gate of ambrosia and moistened all with the rain of Dharma.
Yet, what transgression have I committed to be born in this most evil world of the five turbidities?
I harbor grief and endure suffering, filled with myriad fears that do not leave me for even a moment.
The reason I say this is that I, your disciple, reflect upon my own shallow virtue and meager merit;
the calamities and portents occurring within my dwelling have been frequent and layered.
Evil demons vie with one another day and night to oppress and assail him;
whether sitting or lying down, he finds no peace, as if carrying boiling water or fire within his breast.
Since this recent time, he has lost his wholesome mind and has nothing left to rely upon.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will accept this invitation from your disciple to descend to my dwelling and grant it as a place of peace.
I further request that you command the various deities who guard the house and the taboos of the four seasons to constantly come to protect and defend it,
so that it may always be secure and auspicious day and night, and all calamities and misfortunes may be extinguished.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent!
It shall be as you have said; I myself know the proper time.
At that time, early the next morning, the World-Honored One instructed his disciples.
"You should each adjust your robes and enter the village.
Each of you should take up your alms-bowls and go to the house of the elder's son.
Once the meal is finished, spread out the wheel-turning throne."
He preached the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the elders,
causing them to be free from fear and their bodies and minds to experience joy.
At that time, the Licchavis each gave rise to great gladness.
It was as if a bhikṣu had entered the third dhyāna.
At that time, the World-Honored One immediately called to the various deities who guard the dwelling;
they came to where the Buddha was and he addressed them, saying:
From this day forward, these various gods and ghosts must not recklessly cause alarm or agitation,
nor allow us to remain unsettled or constantly harbor anxiety and fear.
"I shall dispatch powerful spirits and deities to crush and destroy your body, reducing it to fine dust.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the great assembly.
"O sons and daughters of good family,
five hundred years after my parinirvāṇa,
sentient beings will have heavy defilements and false views will blaze ever more fiercely; the paths of Māra will compete to arise, and malevolent spirits will act with delusion."
The gatekeepers each waited for an opportunity to find faults with people and create various obstacles and misfortunes.
At that time, these disciples...
One should single-mindedly recollect the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of bhikṣus.
With pure observance of the precepts, one should uphold the three refuges, the five precepts, the ten wholesome actions, and the eightfold fast-day precepts.
At the six periods of the day and night, perform prostrations and repentance with diligent and earnest resolve.
Invite pure monks to offer a *an-zhai* (peaceful dwelling) vegetarian feast.
Burn various famous incenses and light lamps to maintain a continuous illumination.
Exposing themselves in the central courtyard, they read this sutra.
Since we first established our residence for the summer retreat,
we have constructed the southern veranda, the northern hall, and the eastern and western wings.
Mortars, mills, granaries, storehouses, wells, stoves, gates, and walls;
gardens, groves, ponds, and pools;
and the pens for the six domestic animals—if one moves houses, disturbs the earth, or digs and excavates at improper times; or...
Or one may commit transgressions by disturbing the subduing dragon, the soaring serpent, the Azure Dragon, the White Tiger, the Vermilion Bird, and the Black Tortoise;
or by violating the taboos of the six *jiā* days, the deities of the twelve hours, or the spirits of gates, courtyards, doors, roads, wells, stoves, and dew.
To the deities of the hall, the door, and the latrine:
by the spiritual power of all Buddhas, the majestic radiance of Bodhisattvas, and the power of Prajñāpāramitā,
I now command the guardian deities of the front of the house, the back of the house, the left of the house, the right of the house, and the center of the house, as well as their sons and mothers.
The prohibitions of the Six Jia cycles involving prostrate dragons and soaring serpents;
the deities of the twelve hours, flying corpses, malevolent intrusions, *wangliang* spirits, ghosts, and gods who,
by means of forms and sounds, take refuge in names and attach themselves to one.
From this day forward, you must not recklessly harass my disciples.

You spirits, spirit-mothers, deities within dwellings, malevolent demons, practitioners of sorcery, *wangliang* sprites, and evil māras—each remain in your respective abodes; do not recklessly invade or oppress one another, nor cause them decline or distress.
"Causing such-and-such persons to be startled, shaken, and terrified;
you must act according to my instructions.
If you do not comply with my words, it shall cost you your heads."
He was split into seven pieces like the branches of a tala tree.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
*Namo buddhāya* *Namo dharmāya*
Homage to the Saṃgha. Now, for the sake of this disciple [Name], I shall, by receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, proclaim this divine mantra:
May one-legged beings not afflict me; May two-legged beings not afflict me;
May three-legged beings not afflict me; May four-legged beings not afflict me.
I possess all-encompassing great kindness and great compassion, and I take pity upon all sentient beings.
You evil Māras, each return to your respective domains;
you shall not arbitrarily harass or disturb my disciples.
Furthermore, he spoke the mantra, saying:
"O Śvetabhadra Nāgarāja,
O Subhūti Nāgarāja."
The Dharani for the Boundary-binding of the Naga King Utpala and the Great Naga King Anavatapta:
Gāvaṭi gāvaṭi.
Svāhā! The seven-li boundary of the Great Divine Dragon King of the East.
The Seven- Li Boundary of the Great Nāga King of the Southern Quarter of the Vajra Abode.
The Seven-Li Boundary established by the Great Divine Dragon King of the Western Vajra Abode.
The Seven- Li Boundary of the Great Dragon King of the Northern Diamond Abode.
"Vajra-dhara!
Thus it is said three times: 'O Bhagavan, in the east, seize the necks of the hundred demons with your *śālagrāma* staff and bind them with shackles!
O Bhagavan, in the south, seize the necks of the hundred demons with your *śālagrāma* staff and bind them with shackles!'"
In the western Pāko mountain, Sālaka, seize the necks of the hundred demons and place them in shackles!
In the northern Pāko mountain, Sālaka, seize the necks of the hundred demons and place them in shackles!
Thus it is said three times for those afflicted by illness and those suffering from headaches.
As for the master’s residence and its gates,
you must withdraw all poisons and not disturb my disciples;
if you do not comply with this mantra, your head shall split into seven pieces.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Building houses and establishing halls, To provide for and nurture all living beings;
Creating gardens, groves, and ponds, Along with gates, walls, and latrines."
When the thought arises to build a dwelling, whether moving or still, one should respond to the holy spirit;
bowing the head, take refuge in the Buddha. No demons can shake him;
his bright lamp illuminates the infinite, and through this, the five eyes are born.
The Dharma King’s great mantra-power stirs and shatters billions of Māras;
The Tathāgata’s compassion universally moistens all, his majestic light penetrating the infinite.
Peerless, all take refuge; all malevolent spirits depart of their own accord.
The Buddha addressed the deities of the sun, moon, five planets, and twenty-eight lunar mansions, as well as the devas, nāgas, and ghosts:
"All of you must come and receive these instructions; listen clearly! The Buddha declares:
You must not advance upon or retreat from the household of [Name]."
Or they may construct east and west corridors, south and north wings, and halls;
they command the Generals of the Earth Registry to roam by day and slaughter by night,
as well as the Blue Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, and Black Tortoise.
The years, months, days, and hours bring the prohibitions of the Six Jia;
the Dragon of the Earth Bureau lies dormant—do not move recklessly east or west.
Should there be any movement or stillness, burn incense to announce it.
This dwelling of [Name] is the adamantine ground of the Buddha.
Within a distance of two hundred paces on all sides, the Buddha has made this covenant:
no pestilence-demons or spirits shall dare to trespass.
Those who oppose [this] shall have their heads split into seven pieces;
their bodies shall not remain whole, nor shall they obtain water or grain;
they shall depart from and leave their original palaces and dwellings.
One will already have attained wealth and honor; there will be auspicious changes in fields and agriculture, and one’s great wishes will be fulfilled.
One will travel with glory and distinction while serving in the military.
For those in official service, it is favorable for holding office, and the family lineage will flourish and prosper.
May there be a hundred sons and a thousand grandsons; may fathers be compassionate and children filial.
May men and women be loyal and chaste; may elder brothers be kind and younger brothers be compliant.
May they honor righteousness, benevolence, and worthiness, so that all their wishes are fulfilled as desired.
The ten directions shall bear witness to your practice, such that you attain the Way as a bodhisattva and realize the path as a Buddha.
The Buddha told Ānanda: "If you wish to consecrate a dwelling, leave the central courtyard open and light forty-nine lamps."
Having swept and sprinkled the ground, burned incense, and single-mindedly repented,
he prostrated before the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"What should this sutra be named?
The Buddha said to Ānanda,
"This sutra is named 'The Inconceivable Supernatural Power of the Tathāgata’s Great Compassion.'"

It is also titled "The Buddha-Spoken Sutra on the Divine Incantation for Compassionately Protecting Sentient Beings and Pacifying the Spirits that Destroy Homes. When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the great assembly rejoiced, prostrated themselves, and practiced accordingly.
The *Buddha-spoken Sutra on the Divine Incantation for Pacifying Homes*.
